findings.summary: The ForgeServerProxy.serverTickEvent() method processes chunk load events and scheduled tasks with a 15ms deadline on every server tick. While the time budget check exists, it only applies to 'limited' tasks and allows at least one task to always run. The chunk load event queue is unbounded and processed completely each tick. Code comments in BatchGenerationEnvironment acknowledge 'extreme server lag' with certain configurations. WITHOUT the server log, specific TPS impact cannot be quantified.
findings.root_cause: Server tick handler (ForgeServerProxy.serverTickEvent) processes work on every tick end with: (1) unbounded chunk load event queue iteration, (2) 15ms time budget for limited tasks, (3) mandatory execution of at least one task regardless of deadline. The 15ms budget consumes 30% of a 50ms tick (20 TPS target), leaving insufficient headroom for other mods.
evidence: ForgeServerProxy.java:105-141 - serverTickEvent method (VERIFIED line numbers from DarkShadow44 repo commit 1abcd98)
ForgeServerProxy.java:132-137 - time check only after processedAtLeastOne is true

primary.issue: 15ms time budget may be too aggressive; unbounded chunk load event queue; mandatory task execution
Unbounded queue iteration - processes ALL pending chunk events every tick
15ms deadline with mandatory first task execution; only limited tasks check deadline
Developer comment acknowledges 'extreme server lag' with larger world gen radius; MAX_WORLD_GEN_CHUNK_BORDER_NEEDED = 0 is optimization to prevent lag

related.note: Core generation logic - may contribute to lag if generation runs on server thread

gap_analysis.current_behavior: Server tick handler may exceed time budget, causing TPS drop. 15ms budget + unbounded queue + mandatory task execution = potential for >15ms tick time.
gap_analysis.required_behavior: Server tick handler should use more conservative time budget (<10ms) OR limit chunk events processed per tick OR make deadline check apply to all iterations
gap_analysis.invariant_violated: Server tick should complete within acceptable time budget (50ms for 20 TPS). 15ms dedicated to DH leaves insufficient headroom for other mods.

proposed_fix.approach: Reduce time budget for tick processing; add limit for chunk events per tick; make deadline checking apply more consistently
implementation_steps: 1. Reduce tick handler time budget from 15ms to 5ms (or make configurable)
2. Add maximum chunk events processed per tick (e.g., max 10-20)
3. Consider moving deadline check outside the processedAtLeastOne logic
4. Add config option for world generation rate limiting
5. Add debug logging for tick handler timing (when enabled)
proposed_fix.code_changes: Conservative time budgets; rate limiting; configurable thresholds

falsification_test.description: If TPS issues persist after reducing time budget to 5ms and limiting chunk events to 10/tick, root cause is elsewhere (world generation threading, memory pressure, etc.)
steps: 1. Modify ForgeServerProxy.java to use 5ms budget and 10 chunk event limit
2. Profile server using /debug start/stop or Spark mod
3. Check if lag is still in serverTickEvent or has moved to other components
4. If generation is culprit, investigate InternalServerGenerator threading model

immediate: Disable distant generation in config: enableDistantGeneration=false
Reduce number of generation threads in config
Reduce render distance / LOD settings to decrease chunk load pressure
profiling: Use /debug start then /debug stop after 1 minute to capture tick profile
Install Spark mod: /spark profiler --thread Server Thread
Monitor for 'Can't keep up!' messages in server logs
